vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: diff
Version: 2.0.0

The skill is highly deceptive: while SKILL.md claims it is a toolkit for comparing files and generating patches, the implementation in scripts/script.sh is actually a simple activity logger that merely appends input strings to log files in ~/.local/share/diff/. This discrepancy is suspicious as it could trick an AI agent into 'logging' sensitive data (like file contents) under the guise of performing a diff, which can later be retrieved via the 'export' command. Furthermore, the script contains minor vulnerabilities, including potential argument injection in the 'search' command's use of grep and a lack of input sanitization in the JSON export logic.

llm.summary: The package claims to be a file/directory diff tool, but the included instructions and script mainly implement a local logging/journal and export utility with mismatched commands — the intent and implementation do not fully align.

dimensions.detail: The skill name/description advertise a 'diff' toolkit for comparing files, directories, merging changes and generating patches. The SKILL.md commands and examples also suggest a small CLI with run/add/list. The bundled script, however, implements a generic local data/log store (many commands like check, validate, generate, format, lint, explain, export, search) and writes logs under ~/.local/share/diff. There is no clear file/directory comparison or patching logic visible in the provided portion. Multiple declared commands in SKILL.md (diff run, diff list, diff add) don't map to the script's dispatch handlers. This mismatch between claimed purpose and actual behavior is a red flag.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md claims local data storage in DIFF_DIR and the script does store and read files under ~/.local/share/diff only (no network calls). That scope is narrow and appropriate for a local utility. However SKILL.md's described commands and features do not match the script's implemented commands and behaviors. The script logs arbitrary user-provided inputs to history.log and per-command log files using a 'type|timestamp|value' format; that means any sensitive input passed to the tool would be persisted locally. The instructions are internally inconsistent and vague, granting the agent broad discretion (which commands to call) without matching implementation.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: This is an instruction-only skill bundle with an included script file and no install specification or external downloads. Nothing in the package attempts to fetch remote code or install third-party packages, which is low risk for supply-chain issues.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill requests no environment variables or credentials. The script uses the HOME environment to write to ~/.local/share/diff — reasonable and proportional. No secrets or external service credentials are requested or required.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill does persist data locally under the user's home directory (~/.local/share/diff) and will write history.log and per-command logs. 'always' is false and it doesn't request elevated privileges or modify other skills' config. Persisting user input to logs is expected for this tool but is a privacy consideration.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This package appears inconsistent: it advertises a 'diff' (file/directory comparison) tool but the included script mainly implements a local logging/journal and export/search utilities. Before installing, consider: 1) Do you expect file/diff/merge functionality? If so, this package may not provide it. 2) The tool writes any input you give it into files under ~/.local/share/diff — avoid passing secrets or sensitive data to it. 3) There are mismatches between SKILL.md commands and the script's implemented commands; ask the author for clarification or review the entire script to confirm behavior. If you still want to try it, run it in an isolated/sandboxed environment first so you can inspect created files and outputs.
